title: What Does a System Modify When It Modifies Itself?
abstract: arXiv:2603.27611v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: When a cognitive system modifies its own functioning, what exactly does it modify: a low-level rule, a control rule, or the criterion that evaluates its revisions? Cognitive science describes executive control, metacognition, and hierarchical learning, while artificial intelligence modifies policies, parameters, and learning mechanisms, but the two fields lack common criteria for comparing these transformations. We propose a minimal analytical model distinguishing functional rules Phi_t = {R0, ..., Rk}, modification mechanisms Mt, and evaluation criteria Nt. It separates two independent dimensions: the depth of the modified target and whether the modification is blind or reflexive. Internal representational access AtR and endogenous causal control AtC are further distinguished from external inspectability and modifiability by a designer. translated_title: 系统在修改自身时，究竟修改了什么？
translated_abstract: 当一个认知系统修改自身的运作时，它究竟修改的是什么：是低层规则、控制规则，还是用于评估其修改的标准（判据）？认知科学描述了执行控制、元认知和分层学习，而人工智能领域则修改策略、参数和学习机制，但这两个领域缺乏比较这些转换的共同标准。我们提出了一个最小分析模型，区分功能规则 Φt = {R0, ..., Rk}、修改机制 Mt 和评估标准 Nt。该模型分离出两个相互独立的维度：被修改目标的深度，以及修改是盲目的还是反思性的。此外，内部表征访问 AtR 和内生因果控制 AtC 进一步区别于设计者所拥有的外部可检视性与可修改性。由修改目标所定义的四种模式包括：不涉及组织性修改的行动……（摘要不完整）
tldr: 该论文提出一个区分功能规则、修改机制与评估标准的最小分析模型，通过“修改目标深度”与“盲目或反思性修改”两个独立维度，为统一比较认知科学与人工智能中的自我修改提供了分析框架。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a minimal analytical model distinguishing functional rules, modification mechanisms, and evaluation criteria, which—via two independent dimensions of modification depth and blind versus reflexive modification—offers a unified framework for comparing self-modification across cognitive science and AI.
